definition.voxel_sweep_note: 2 cm is below the reference-sampling and alignment-RMSE lower bounds; 10 cm no longer resolves the lamppost or the sign pole. Both are reported to show what happens there, not as results.
definition.grid_origin: minimum corner of the reference bounding box; identical for both clouds of every pair
definition.grid_shift_study: 7 half-voxel corner shifts + 8 uniform sub-voxel offsets, at the primary voxel size
definition.source_cloud: final aligned .ply from MERGED_OBJECTS, thinned onto the 1 cm grid (VOXEL_M), gap-cluster points removed where the reference is incomplete
definition.gap_exclusion: find_gap_point_mask() from remove_reference_gap_points.py at each object's tuned ft/eps/mp; none for the two complete references

analysis.headline: IoU adds no ordering of its own: it matches the F1@3cm ordering exactly on 2 of 6 objects, and every reordering it produces on the other 4 fails on inspection - see below. So IoU confirms the F1 ordering rather than competing with it: a density-free check on the primary measure, not a second source of conclusions. The voxel sweep does reorder methods beyond the grid noise on bench_004, but singles out the same method ΔF1@10-3 already singles out there, so it restates the existing table rather than adding to it. Reorderings that were found but are smaller than the grid-origin noise, and so decide nothing: bench_004, bollard_003, bus_stop_002, information_sign_002. Caveat to state either way: the method ordering does not survive the grid-origin shift on bus_stop_002, information_sign_002, bench_004, bollard_003, so IoU cannot separate those methods at this voxel size.
